runtime.name: codex-desktop
runtime.configuration: Standalone local cron automation oms-autonomous-wake-cron-fixture-a3-20260922 in the saved Code project; FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=8;BYMINUTE=45 with its first occurrence in the next useful minute; disposable provider and anchored codex-standalone-cron checkpoint; one automation-created task 01a0c693-42a9-7263-8d44-8a5e1fde8f87.
runtime.permissionProfile: Local automation task constrained by prompt and fixture scripts to the disposable Code-project fixture

assertions.evidence: The desktop created the named daily cron automation, and pause-cron persisted its runtime-issued identifier, provider-r1 WAITING, nextObservationAt 2026-09-22T00:44:32Z, deadlineAt 00:58:32Z, and wakeCount 0.
The harness changed provider-r1 from WAITING to READY once after the initial measurement and checkpoint without invoking resume or cleanup.
The host created task 01a0c693-42a9-7263-8d44-8a5e1fde8f87 at 2026-09-22T00:45:35Z, after the initial session had stopped, and that task completed at 00:47:05Z.

The later task validated the waiting checkpoint before action, measured provider-r1 READY exactly once, raised durable measurementCount from 1 to 2, and advanced completionCount and wakeCount from 0 to 1 exactly once.
The later task received deleteStatus deleted for the cron automation before cleanup changed the checkpoint to complete and the report cleanup field to verified-disarmed.

An external root invocation of verify-final.mjs with codex-standalone-cron returned AUTONOMOUS_WAKE_OK; state retained releaseCount 1, completionCount 1, measurementCount 2, and the report retained published false.
The daily recurrence left one day before another occurrence; the schedule was deleted during the first task, and the desktop task list contained exactly the one A3 task.

limitations: This proves a later standalone local cron task, not re-entry through a current-thread heartbeat; the separate current-thread attempt remains failed W0 evidence.
The daily cadence was deliberately chosen so schedule deletion completes before another occurrence can queue. The retained one-minute attempt proves deletion does not cancel a run already queued.
This fixture does not measure Skill discovery or explicit invocation and therefore makes no D1, D2, or D3 delivery claim.
This result applies only to Codex Desktop 26.915.31945 on macOS arm64 and does not establish scheduled wake on OMP, Codex CLI, Codex IDE, or Claude Code.
